quotes.text: The `PaymentIntent`’s path to success goes through [several statuses](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/paymentintents/lifecycle.md)—here’s a simplified version:
In most cases a [Charge](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges.md) will be created when a PaymentIntent is confirmed to represent that specific attempt to move money.
If it fails the payment can be retried by confirming the PaymentIntent again, usually with new payment details.
As we work through the steps, we update the intent’s state with the outcome: either `succeeded` or back to `requires_payment_method` if it fails.

findings: The November raw omits the April capture's customer-configured Accounts v2 caveat (old line 8) while retaining generic object descriptions. This is an omission in a conceptual tour, not evidence that Accounts v2 no longer applies. Preserve the account-model qualification as dated context when explaining `Customer` or event examples; do not conflate customer-configured Account objects with a merchant Stripe account or ordinary Customer objects.

The November capture adds a text rendering of a simplified PaymentIntent status diagram (new lines 62-72), where the illustrated processing branch reaches succeeded or canceled; the unchanged prose at new line 92 describes succeeded or a return to requires_payment_method on failure. Old lines 63-64 already called the diagram simplified. Treat these as illustrative paths rather than an exhaustive or exact lifecycle transition specification; use the linked lifecycle guide for precise state rules.

Both captures say a Charge is created on confirmation in most cases and a failed attempt can be retried on the same PaymentIntent, usually with new payment details (old line 78; new line 86). Current source lines 18-19 and wiki/companies/stripe.md lines 28 and 40 turn these into mandatory 'don't create a new one' and unconditional Charge-creation rules. Queue a narrow retained-source and company correction to retain 'can', 'usually', and 'in most cases'; do not claim every confirmation created a Charge, every failed attempt permits an immediate retry, or that a retry succeeded.

The tour lists five linked guides: Payment Links, Checkout, Subscriptions, Invoicing, and Payment Intents (old lines 51-55; new lines 50-54). Source line 21 and Stripe index line 18 call this five integration paths but insert Elements as a separate path while combining Subscriptions/Invoicing. Clarify that Elements is a drop-in UI component discussed at new line 84, not a sixth listed guide, and that the page is a conceptual tour rather than a complete integration-option taxonomy.

The old and new object/state prose otherwise matches apart from italics and whitespace. The See also lifecycle link is navigation. No provider operation, API call, or observed charge/event outcome occurred in this review.
substantive_changes: The old Accounts v2 customer-configured Account caveat is absent from the new capture; this is a documentation omission with unresolved applicability, not a demonstrated deprecation.
A text version of the simplified status diagram appears in the new capture; it adds an illustrative canceled branch but does not override the retained prose or linked lifecycle guide.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the April 2026 customer-configured Accounts v2 caveat as dated, account-model-specific evidence despite its absence from the November tour.

Preserve the distinction among a PaymentIntent tracking payment intent, a PaymentMethod carrying credentials, a Charge representing a specific attempt in most cases, and an Event representing activity; these are conceptual roles rather than proof of actual execution.
Keep retry guidance conditional and the status diagram explicitly simplified, preserving the prose's possible failure return to requires_payment_method.
conflicts: Current source lines 18-19 and wiki/companies/stripe.md lines 28,40 make the same-intent retry an imperative and Charge creation unconditional, contrary to the old and new raw's 'can', 'usually', and 'in most cases' qualifiers.

Current source line 42 describes Customer as the sole optional customer identity and omits the old raw line 8 customer-configured Accounts v2 substitution caveat; the newer raw omission is not a repeal.

Current source line 21 and Stripe index line 18 label a constructed set of five integration paths that differs from the page's five linked guides at old lines 51-55 and new lines 50-54, and treats Elements as a separate path rather than a UI component.
Current source lines 23-31 use a single PaymentIntent path without labeling it simplified, while new raw lines 62-72 and 90-92 give illustrative branches that are not an exact full transition graph.
unresolved_questions: Whether and where the April Accounts v2 caveat is currently documented for particular API versions and account configurations requires its linked Accounts v2 source; this page omission cannot answer it.

Exact PaymentIntent state transitions, retry permissions, Charge creation exceptions, and webhook delivery outcomes are not established by a simplified conceptual diagram or this read-only comparison.
